extracted.intended_audience: journalists, news managers, journalism students, media scholars, educators, and media professionals interested in local television news and race/ethnicity coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or researching local television news coverage—particularly how and why local newscasts cover (or fail to cover) people of color and the newsroom practices that shape that coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of local news (relevance to communities)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the purpose of local news is to cover individual communities and to present issues of interest and concern to local audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a newscast's stories reflect the specific interests, concerns, and events of the local communities it serves rather than generic or nationally-oriented content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localism vs. homogenization of newscasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Why are local newscasts so similar in markets around the country?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether coverage demonstrates meaningful local variation. Homogeneity across markets is a negative indicator—look for stories, frames, and priorities that mirror national templates rather than local conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful coverage of people of color
rubrics_metrics.description: Local television news coverage of people of color does not occur in more meaningful ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether coverage of minority communities is substantive (context, depth, routine inclusion) rather than superficial or tokenistic. Check frequency, story placement, and narrative depth about minority communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of racism and ethnicity among newsroom personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Heider examines the perceptions of racism and ethnicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate newsroom attitudes and beliefs that shape story selection and framing. Consider interviews/observations showing how staff perceive race/ethnicity and how those perceptions influence editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘White news’ decision-making vs representational appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Dichotomy: 'white' news (content determined by white managers) being delivered by non-white news anchors, thus giving the appearance of 'non-white' news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess who sets the news agenda (managers, producers) versus who appears on screen. Distinguish between surface-level diversity (on-air faces) and substantive editorial diversity (who decides story priorities). Watch for tokenism where representation masks uniform content priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of coverage on viewers' perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: How coverage of minorities influences viewers' perceptions of their minority neighbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure or reason about downstream effects: whether story selection and framing contribute to stereotypes, fear, misunderstanding, or accurate knowledge. Consider audience studies or plausible effects based on content patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incognizant racism (patterns of omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incognizant racism—as a way of explaining how news workers consistently ignore news in significant portions of the communities they cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for systematic omissions of communities, issues, or sources. Evaluate routines, beats, and geographic/cultural blind spots that lead to consistent undercoverage rather than overt discriminatory intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managerial responsibility and newsroom structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of station owners and news managers who ultimately have the first and last word on how the TV newsrooms are run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organizational structures, decision hierarchies, and policies. Determine whether management practices, staffing, and resource allocation enable or hinder inclusive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency and suitability (research quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of ethnographic study and participant observation; detailed methodology included as an appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research evaluating newsrooms, check for clear description of methods (participant observation, sample markets), researcher access, and appendices providing methodology detail. Methodological rigor and transparency strengthen claims about newsroom practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable remedies and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible Remedies; Heider offers remedies and 'solid, common sense solutions' to improve coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposals for correcting coverage deficiencies for practicality, specificity, and managerial applicability. Favor remedies that address editorial decision-making, staffing, beats, training, and policies rather than only surface-level changes.
